statement: Prime-Error Distributional Temperedness Equivalence Theorem: For the normalized Chebyshev prime-counting error E(u) = exp(-u/2)(psi(exp u) - exp u), the regular distribution T_E defined on D(R) = C_c^infinity(R) extends continuously to a tempered distribution in S'(R) if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds. The three conditions (A) RH, (B) pointwise polynomial growth E(u) = O((1+u)^N) for some N, and (C) distributional temperedness T_E in S'(R) are mutually equivalent: (A) <=> (B) <=> (C). Direction (A) => (B) => (C) follows from von Koch (1901) and Cramer (1919), where RH forces N = 2. Direction (C) => (A) is proved via Route II: for a smooth cutoff chi with chi = 0 on (-infty, 0.1] and chi = 1 on [0.5, infty), E_chi(u) = chi(u)E(u) is supported in [0.1, infty). For u <= 0, psi(exp u) = 0 so E(u) = -exp(u/2) != 0; the tail (1-chi)E is in S(R) (smooth and exponentially decaying as u -> -infty, with support unbounded toward -infty). The pairing <T_{E_chi}, exp(-zu)> is defined rigorously for Re(z) > 0 via <T_{E_chi}, rho(u)exp(-zu)> for any smooth extension rho identically 1 on [0, infty) and vanishing on (-infty, -0.5], independent of rho. By the Schwartz-Laplace theorem (Schwartz 1951, Tome II Chap. VIII Thm I; Hormander 1983, Vol. I Thm 7.4.2), T_E in S'(R) forces L[E_chi](z) to be holomorphic on the entire half-plane Re(z) > 0. For Re(z) > 1/2, L[E_chi](z) = G(z) - H(z), where G(z) = -1/(z+1/2) * (zeta'/zeta)(z+1/2) - 1/(z-1/2) and H(z) = int_0^0.5 (chi(u) - 1_{[0,infty)}(u)) E(u) exp(-zu) du is an entire function whose integrand (chi - 1_{[0,infty)})E is supported strictly in the compact interval [0, 0.5]. Any nontrivial zero rho = 1/2 + delta + i*gamma with delta > 0 produces an isolated pole at z_rho = delta + i*gamma in Re(z) > 0 with non-zero residue -m_rho/rho != 0, contradicting holomorphy. Therefore, delta <= 0 for all zeros, forcing RH. Route I does not derive the required polynomial slow-decrease hypothesis unconditionally. Lean formalizes exact local algebraic identities and pole residues, while the Schwartz-Laplace theorem and prime-error asymptotics are cited external theorems. Distributional temperedness is thus an RH-equivalent criterion rather than an independent TC bridge.

T_E is the regular distribution <T_E, phi> = int_R E(u) phi(u) du on D(R)

object_studied: Regular distribution T_E of the normalized Chebyshev prime error and its half-line Laplace transform L[E_chi](z)
fourier_normalization: Additive Fourier-Laplace transform on R; Schwartz space S(R) with seminorms p_{alpha,beta}
multiplicity_convention: Nontrivial zero multiplicity m_rho >= 1 and von Mangoldt weights Lambda(n)
measure_and_window: Additive Lebesgue measure du on R; unweighted Schwartz test space S(R); smooth half-line window chi
order_of_limits: Laplace parameter limit Re(z) -> 0+; asymptotic growth limits u -> +/- infty
exact_conclusion: T_E extends to a tempered distribution in S'(R) if and only if the Riemann Hypothesis holds: (A) <=> (B) <=> (C). In particular, distributional temperedness genuinely forces delta = 0 for all zeros.
logical_negation: T_E in S'(R) with an off-critical zero delta > 0, or RH holds while T_E is non-tempered, or E(u) satisfies polynomial slow decrease unconditionally without an a priori prime bound (FALSIFIED / REFUTED)
falsification_attempts: Gate 1 & 4 (Root and Pole Analysis): proved that the pole of -(1/s)*(zeta'/zeta)(s) at s = 1 has residue +1, which cancels identically with -1/(z-1/2), making z = 1/2 a removable singularity in Re(z) > 0

Gate 5 (Dominance and Non-Cancellation): proved that for any off-critical zero rho = 1/2 + delta + i*gamma with delta > 0, the residue Res(G, z_rho) = -m_rho/rho has magnitude m_rho/|rho| > 0, which cannot cancel with any entire function H(z) supported on [0, 0.5]

Gate 3 & 9 (Adversarial Holomorphy Contradiction): tested against Schwartz (1951, Tome II Chap. VIII Thm I) and Hormander (1983, Vol I Thm 7.4.2), proving that if T_E in S'(R), the Laplace transform L[E_chi](z) must be holomorphic in Re(z) > 0, which directly refutes the existence of any off-critical pole with delta > 0

Gate 6 & 7 (Route I Slow Decrease Obstruction): evaluated downward slope E'(u) = -exp(u/2) - (1/2)*E(u) ~ -exp(u/2) between prime powers, proving that Route I does not derive polynomial slow decrease unconditionally without assuming an RH-equivalent bound

Gate 8 (Phase-Cancelling Test Construction): tested against eta_n(u) = exp(-i*gamma*u)*exp(-u^2/(2n^2)), proving that <phi_lambda, eta_n> = sqrt(2*pi)*n*exp(n^2*delta^2/2) diverges super-polynomially over all Schwartz seminorms p_{alpha,beta}(eta_n) <= C(alpha,beta,gamma)*n^alpha for delta != 0

Gate 10 (Equivalence and Circularity Audit): established that while (C) => (A) is mathematically rigorous, deriving (C) from prime arithmetic unconditionally is equivalent to solving RH, confirming that temperedness is not an independent TC shortcut
